canonicalMutationReview.registrationPolicy: Do not register mutants against source absent from the verification head. Add them after integration so kills prove the actual merged guard.

postal: authenticated delivery-failed/bounced/DNS lifecycle proves provider acceptance of the original submission and must not reopen resend eligibility
normalized webhook lifecycle cannot be shadowed by arbitrary payload.status
NOT_FOUND cannot automatically release an uncertain external effect
payment: first-cash fulfilment requires canonical payment reconciliation
payment truth digest is recomputed and must match canonical reconciliation state
post-reconciliation edits cannot pass via a merely 64-hex-looking digest
a sixth qualified conversation after zero paid pilot is blocked by KILL_OR_RETHINK
genome: runtime route must be admitted and selected in the mission bundle
dependency closure is evaluated after bundle construction
negative cost or latency telemetry cannot dominate routing
out-of-range quality reliability or success telemetry cannot manufacture a winner
duplicate capability IDs or canonical capability identities fail the Genome doctor closed

truthRules: A zero-step workflow failure is environment evidence, not source failure evidence.
A retry that also produces zero steps strengthens the environment-startup classification but still proves nothing about source correctness.
No mutation kill is counted unless the mutated source actually executes and the intended suite fails for the intended reason.
Exact-head proof is SHA-scoped and expires when the branch advances.
No commercial truth changes without real external evidence.
nextVerificationActions: Retry the latest verification head only when runner execution becomes available; avoid manufacturing repeated noise while runner startup is uniformly failing.
When Postal, Payment, and Genome source reach an integration candidate, add the refreshed high-consequence guards to scripts/mutation-war.mjs and require canonical kills.
Require exact-head PostgreSQL execution before concurrency claims, and exact-head browser execution before browser-path claims.
Keep PR #321 draft until real step-level evidence exists.
